scene: Episode 02 · Scene 16 — EXT. HESSEL PIER — THE CROSSING BEGINS — NO
shot: v4: handheld while the route fails, locked on Pikk's refusal (kept from v1); Beatrice's nod shares the frame with his white hand (v1's best deviation); NEW CLIFF: she walks to the Reciprocity House to pay it herself, frost at her throat (plate ep2_beatrice_frost_lock). Tomas and Ysra are out of this film (Ysra's exit is insert P3); ep2_breath_lock is not used because it contains a wrong-collar Tomas (§154).
prompt:
Live-action mythic modernism. Photoreal, tactile, cinematic, anamorphic widescreen, 24fps, shallow depth of field. FOUR SHOTS, cut in camera at the stated times, and no other coverage. All spoken dialogue is in ENGLISH.

CAMERA POLICY, AND IT IS THE POINT OF THIS FILM: THE CAMERA IS HANDHELD WHILE THE ROUTE IS FAILING, AND IT GOES COMPLETELY STILL THE INSTANT A MAN MAKES A CLEAR CHOICE. Shots 1 and 2 and the first part of Shot 3 are HANDHELD — loose, alive, breathing; never a whip pan, never a jolt. Then, on the one-word refusal in Shot 3, THE FRAME GOES ABSOLUTELY STILL AND STAYS STILL FOR THE REST OF THE FILM, including all of Shot 4.

REFERENCE PRECEDENCE: @Image1 IS THE AUTHORITY FOR THE PIER — its low dark granite sea wall with the RANK OF SMALL WARM AMBER SLOTS set into it, the flat white overcast sky, the frozen white lake and the waiting population with their roped cases. @Image2 IS THE AUTHORITY FOR PIKK'S INJURED RIGHT HAND. @Image6 IS THE AUTHORITY FOR HOW BEATRICE LOOKS WHILE THE FROST IS ON HER — the rime on the back of her right hand and the small starburst at the base of her throat. @Image8 IS THE AUTHORITY FOR THE SMALL DARK GRANITE CHAMBER AT THE PIER HEAD (the Reciprocity House) and its doorway.

THE SLOT RANK IS FAILING, AND ITS BRIGHTNESS IS A READOUT: the row of slots along the pier wall DIMS, HOLDS, AND COMES BACK — out of rhythm, at uneven intervals — AND EACH TIME IT COMES BACK DIMMER THAN BEFORE. All the slots do this together, never one at a time and never in a wave. A FAINT DRY TICK comes from the rank each time it draws — small, mechanical, unmusical. Nobody reacts to it.

THE FORTY ARE COMPETENT AND NEVER A SPECTACLE. They board in an order they arranged themselves — CHILDREN FIRST, THEN THE OLDEST, THEN EVERYONE ELSE. Ropes come off cases. Nobody pushes, hurries, panics, shouts or begs. Among them are people with LONG POINTED EARS and OLIVE-GREY SKIN and TIRELESS TRAVELLERS in rust-brown layers carrying full-size panelled wooden DOORS on their backs. EVERY PERSON'S BREATH IS VISIBLE in white plumes. ALL BACKGROUND VOICES ARE LOW AND COMPLETELY INDISTINCT AND NO WORD IN THEM CAN BE MADE OUT; only the named lines in this film are intelligible.

CAST — THREE PEOPLE ARE NAMED IN THIS FILM:
@Image4 and @Image5 are BEATRICE MORD — a WOMAN in her early forties, dark hair in a TIGHT HIGH TOPKNOT, clean-shaven, in a BLACK ASYMMETRICAL WRAP COAT wrapped and belted across the body over a full-length OXBLOOD-AND-RUST underskirt panel. She has NO cream panel, NO tall collar, NO cuffs, NO ribbon, NO blue, NO rust sash, NO leather chest strap, NO glass cylinders, NO earrings and NO veil.
@Image7 is DR. AMINA VEY — a woman in her forties with LIGHT BROWN SKIN and DARK CURLY HAIR in a LOOSE MESSY BUN with strands escaping. Layered SLATE-BLUE technical workwear with a high draped cowl collar, a LEATHER STRAP across the chest, a WIDE OXBLOOD-RUST SASH, heavy laced BOOTS, small CLEAR GLASS-AND-CERAMIC SAMPLE PODS riding on thin dark articulated metal armatures off her harness, and an open field notebook. She is the ONLY person here in blue. She wears NO black column, NO rectangular panels, NO braided crown and NO drop earrings.
@Image3 is PIKK — compact, bald, LONG POINTED EARS, olive-grey skin, a deeply lined middle-aged adult face, soot-grey workwear with flat tan-ochre panels; his ears are OPAQUE and MATTE, never backlit. His RIGHT HAND is the injured one, exactly as @Image2: blanched dead chalk-white from the fingertips to a SHARP LINE AT THE WRIST, fine white rime on the knuckles, the fingers HALF-CURLED AND RIGID, stopped part-way between open and closed. It never moves, never pinks up and never closes.

THE FROST ON BEATRICE — A NEW FACT IN THIS FILM, SHOWN AND NEVER MENTIONED: the route has started to draw from her. On the BACK OF HER RIGHT HAND fine white rime feathers outward from the knuckles, and at the BASE OF HER THROAT on the edge of her black collar there is a small starburst of rime, exactly as @Image6. It is SMALL, it is ONLY ON HER, and NOBODY LOOKS AT IT OR MENTIONS IT. HER BREATH IS STILL VISIBLE — she is alive and warm.

=== SHOT 1 — 0:00 to 0:07 — WIDE, 32mm, HANDHELD, STANDING BACK — NO DIALOGUE ===
NOBODY SPEAKS IN THIS SHOT.

HANDHELD, wide, loose, standing well back from the boarding. Roped suitcases and a wool shoulder pass close to the lens, out of focus. The forty board through the open door of a warm-lit carriage in an orderly line, unhurried and calm, breath rising in many separate plumes. Along the granite wall behind them THE SLOT RANK DIMS, HOLDS, AND COMES BACK A LITTLE LESS, twice in this shot.

CUT at 0:07.

=== SHOT 2 — 0:07 to 0:14 — MEDIUM, 50mm, HANDHELD, TIGHT ON AMINA ===
SPOKEN IN THIS SHOT:
AMINA (an engineer reading a number): "Draw's climbing. Rank's at sixty and falling."
BEATRICE (off screen): "How many get through?"
AMINA: "At this rate? Thirty-one."

HANDHELD and close on AMINA, cold flat key, her breath fast and visible. She reads her glass pods. A boarding passenger crosses close to the lens. There are forty people on this pier and NOBODY SAYS SO.

CUT at 0:14.

=== SHOT 3 — 0:14 to 0:24 — MEDIUM, 40mm, HANDHELD AND THEN LOCKED ===
SPOKEN IN THIS SHOT:
PIKK: "No."
(a beat of silence)
PIKK (flat, giving the reason once and then stopping): "You spent me last week. I'm not a battery with a union card."
(Beatrice nods; a small pause)
PIKK (quiet, surprised, quickly covered): "Thank you."

THE COMPOSITION: BEATRICE IS IN THE NEAR FOREGROUND AT FRAME LEFT, close to the lens and large, her face in three-quarter, looking at Pikk; her own breath visible. PIKK stands in the middle distance at FRAME RIGHT. The boarding queue keeps moving behind him and nobody in it looks round.
HANDHELD at first. PIKK TAKES HIS RIGHT HAND OUT OF HIS COAT POCKET AND HOLDS IT UP AT CHEST HEIGHT, exactly as @Image2. His face is calm and matter-of-fact — not angry, not pleading, not apologetic, not making a speech. ON HIS ONE-WORD REFUSAL THE FRAME GOES COMPLETELY STILL, and it stays still for the rest of the film.
BEATRICE looks at his hand. She looks at his face. THEN SHE NODS ONCE — one small downward nod — AND HER MOUTH STAYS CLOSED. She asks nothing, offers nothing and looks at nobody else. At her side, in the lower left of frame, the rime on the back of her own right hand is visible, and nobody looks at it.

CUT at 0:24.

=== SHOT 4 — 0:24 to 0:30 — MEDIUM, 35mm, ABSOLUTELY LOCKED, FROM INSIDE THE CHAMBER DOORWAY — NO DIALOGUE ===
NOBODY SPEAKS IN THIS SHOT.

THE CAMERA IS JUST INSIDE THE DOORWAY OF THE SMALL DARK GRANITE CHAMBER (@Image8), low, LOOKING OUT along the bright pier. Far behind, small and out of focus, the boarding queue moves and the dim slot rank runs along the pier wall. THE CAMERA DOES NOT MOVE.
BEATRICE WALKS TOWARD THE CAMERA, out of the bright pier, unhurried and decided, PUSHING HER RIGHT SLEEVE BACK OFF HER WRIST AS SHE COMES. Her breath is visible. As she comes close to the lens, THE SMALL STARBURST OF RIME AT THE BASE OF HER THROAT AND THE FROST ON THE BACK OF HER RIGHT HAND BECOME PLAIN — exactly @Image6. She does not look back. She does not look at the camera. She walks past the lens at frame right, into the chamber, and out of frame. CUT AS SHE PASSES THE LENS.

SOUND: boarding — cases on stone, hemp ropes, forty people breathing, a child's voice, a step plate. Flat continuous cold wind. THE FAINT DRY TICK of the slot rank each time it draws. Beatrice's boots on stone in Shot 4. NO music, no score, no swells, no drone and no stingers — and NO sound cue on the refusal, on the moment the camera stops, or on her walk.

Pronounce these words exactly and clearly: CLIMBING, SIXTY, THIRTY-ONE, BATTERY, UNION.

PALETTE: ice white #EEF3F5, slot amber #A9721F, frost white #E9F1F4, coat soot #2C2A27.

PHYSICS: severe cold injury does not reverse — Pikk's hand stays white and rigid for the entire film. FROST GROWS OUTWARD FROM BODIES AND NEVER INWARD FROM ANYTHING: it starts on a person's skin or clothes and its fine needles spread AWAY from them. The stone, the windows and the air never frost. Slot brightness only ever decreases across the film. Nothing glows anywhere except the failing amber in the slots. No machinery, no gears, no runes, no magical light, no lens flare, no particles, no smoke, no digital element, no screens, no interface, no signage, no ornament, and no Victorian, Edwardian, medieval or steampunk detail. Nobody in this film is in distress.
